Wrangle Report¶

1 Intro¶

Here, we will briefly highlight particular topics tackled during the wrangling process that we have applied in wrangle_act.ipynb and document additional tests that have been performed but are not part of the 'data wrangling' process itself.

2 Gather¶

We have gathered data in the following ways:

  • Tweet Data from twitter_archive_enhanced.csv;
  • API Data from tweet_json.txt - (no API key available; no answer from Twitter concerning the developer account request);
  • Image Predictions from Requests' HTTPS request.

Notes follow (2.1 to 2.3).

2.1 Trim Postponed¶

Right after having imported the 'twitter_archive_enhanced.csv', I have thought of filtering out tweets that do not meet the 'key-point' specifications - $i.e.$:

  • You only want original ratings (no retweets)...
  • ...that have images.
  • You do not need to gather the tweets beyond August $1^{st}$, 2017.

However, I have decided to postpone these operations to the 'Cleaning' stage, for this step would require both, an assessment and a manipulation of the datasets.

2.2 JSON Data Load into a Pandas Data Frame¶

I have noticed that data types are processed differently if JSON data are imported via json.loads method or by using Pandas' read_json method.

In particular, I have tried to import the file tweet_json.txt in two ways:

  1. By opening the file, transforming each JSON object in a dictionary, and adding it singularly into the target Pandas data frame ( DS['api'], as in wrangle_act.ipynb);
  2. By importing the whole file directly with Pandas' read_json method (api_bkp).

For each of them, I have achieved the following results.

  • Documentation for 2.:

  • DTypes Comparison

  • Non-matching Records

  • Original Data

It looks like Pandas' import via json.loads processes the data in accordance with the original .json file.

This issue should be investigated further.

However, we will not proceed further, for this lays out of the scope of this project.

2.3 Import Check for Image Predictions¶

3 Assess¶

The programmatical assessment took place in full for the Twitter Archive, whereas it has been limited to the columns actually used of the API data (retweet_count, and favorite_count for tweet IDs contained in the trimmed version of the Enhanced Twitter Archive).

For image_predictions we posed more focus on the relation between tweets and image links, and between breed kind and its detection in the p1_dog, p2_dog, p3_dog columns.

4 Clean¶

We have cleaned each issue identified during the assessment stage by iteratively defining the issue, coding the related cleaning process and testing the result.

We have removed columns containing 'NaN's only.

While tackling issue 'Cleanness - 6, 7', we have integrated numerators from tweet text and corrected float entries (handled with rounding). Numerators and denominators have been normalized.

In 'Cleanness - 8', we have removed wrong names, found other missing names, and integrated them. (Names found where the actual name was following the word 'named').

We mapped columns doggo, floofer, pupper, puppo into a new, unique column dog_stages. This latter contains stages of dogs in each tweet. In doing so, we can keep the same observational unit (tweets) in the master data frame.

5 Store, Analyze, and Visualize¶

We counted ratings per day and derived average rating values per weekday from the timestamp directly by leveraging on Pandas' datetime methods. We have visually analyzed a graph of the daily tweet frequeny over time.
